commands.name: document_open
commands.description: Opens an image or PDF in Preview, or brings it to the front if it's open.

args.name: path
args.meaning: An absolute path, or one starting with ~, to an image (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .heic, .tif, .tiff, .gif, .bmp) or a PDF.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": Preview has no scripting for this.

commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: The document is in front in Preview; the file is unchanged.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the change wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: the document has a dialog open, a dialog with typed text is showing, or another app came to the front; nothing is changed

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: nothing is at the path; nothing is changed

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: PREVIEW_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it; nothing is done

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode is "background": there is no background mode

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with Preview 11.0 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
Only touches what PREVIEW_ALLOWED_ROOT allows if it is set; if it isn't set, any image or PDF you can reach is accepted.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
Preview may open it as a tab of another window; the tab is chosen by its file name.

Cut off the right third of the image
Crop this screenshot to the top half
